findings.claim: Bumping the cache `version` invalidates every previously written on-disk cache, but nothing in this change appears to purge the now-orphaned cache directories/metadata from the old version.
findings.rationale: This field is almost certainly part of the cache key/path (that is the usual reason for such a bump). If old version-scoped directories are not garbage-collected elsewhere, each bump leaves a stale copy of the entire module cache on disk, growing unboundedly across releases. Medium confidence — cleanup may well exist in code outside this hunk (e.g. driven by `metadataFilePath`), so this is worth a quick check rather than a definite bug.

findings.claim: The version is a hardcoded literal that must be manually kept in sync with any change to the cache format/serialization; a forgotten bump silently yields corrupt or mis-typed cache hits.
findings.rationale: Hardcoded invalidation tokens are fragile: the correctness of the whole cache depends on a human remembering to edit this line whenever the persisted shape or key-generation logic changes. Low-to-medium confidence that this is actionable here (the bump itself looks correct and intentional), but it is a real behavioral hazard worth flagging — deriving it from the package version or a hash of the serializer would be safer.
